steps.prompt: Before the check: which sentence type do you find easiest to write, and which one do you want more practice with?

cards.title: The four types: quick review
cards.body: Simple: one independent clause. Compound: two independent clauses (comma + FANBOYS, or a semicolon). Complex: one independent + a dependent clause (because, when, although, who, which…). Compound-complex: two independents + a dependent.

cards.title: Variety and clarity: quick review
cards.body: Mix types, lengths and openers. Combine choppy short sentences. Split stringy and/so sentences and anything past about 40 words. Save short simple sentences for your key points.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First, a 10-question quiz: you need 8 right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see which skills to review, and you’ll get new questions next time. Then you’ll write a paragraph that uses all four sentence types. Quill gives it a score.

prompts: Look at your sentence map. Which type did you use most, and was that a good choice?
What will you check in your sentences every time you write an essay?
